s1.syndrome_frame: febrile illness with rash and hypotension in an immunocompromised patient
salient_findings: erythematous patches and thin plaques with telangiectases and hyperpigmentation
intravascular atypical cells on skin biopsy
key_facts: patient is a woman in her 50s
history of chronic pulmonary coccidiomycosis
being treated with fluconazole
admitted for fever, hypotension, and rash
previous reaction to pembrolizumab
new skin eruption is widespread and asymptomatic
skin eruption has been ongoing for 1 to 2 weeks
white blood cell count is 4100/μL
absolute neutrophil count is 2940/μL
hemoglobin level is 8.2 g/dL
platelet count is 62 ×10^3/μL
blood culture results show no growth at 1 week
serum β-D-glucan, galactomannan, Coccidioides antibody, and immunodiffusion results are negative
respiratory viral panel and SARS-CoV-2 test results are negative

raw.rationale: The presence of intravascular atypical cells on skin biopsy, as shown by hematoxylin-eosin stained sections and CD56 immunostaining, is a key diagnostic feature of intravascular large B cell lymphoma. This finding, combined with the patient's symptoms of fever, hypotension, and rash, supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: mycosis fungoides
rejected.why: Mycosis fungoides typically presents with more localized skin lesions and does not typically involve intravascular atypical cells on biopsy.

rejected.label: skin rash
rejected.why: Skin rash is a symptom rather than a diagnosis and does not explain the patient's other symptoms or biopsy findings.

rejected.label: febrile illness
rejected.why: Febrile illness is a nonspecific term that does not account for the patient's specific symptoms or biopsy results.

rejected.label: vasculitis
rejected.why: Vasculitis can cause skin lesions and systemic symptoms, but the presence of intravascular atypical cells on biopsy is more suggestive of intravascular large B cell lymphoma.
